LESSON: GUIDED READING: EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.5 Guided Reading: Reading Aloud (2 Sessions) • Articulation • Verbal c
Topic 2.7: Guided Reading: Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Reading: Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is reading important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning
2. create a reading log to monitor reading activities

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED READING: EXTENSIVE READING
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Reading: Extensive Reading helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED READING: EXTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading: Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a reading log to monitor reading activities

What this means
In this part you learn to create a reading log to monitor reading activities. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a reading log to monitor reading activities.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading: Extensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a reading log to monitor reading activities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Reading: Extensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading: Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading: Extensive Reading to a partner. (skill: create a reading log to monitor reading activities)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Reading: Extensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning.
3. Practise this skill: create a reading log to monitor reading activities.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Reading: Extensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Reading: Extensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Guided Reading: Extensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is reading important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Reading: Extensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning.
5. Be able to: create a reading log to monitor reading activities.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
